(Per: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE RAJEEV RANJAN PRASAD)
12 27-02-2026 Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.
2. The prayer for suspension of sentence and release of the appellant on bail is pending consideration before this Court since long.
3. Earlier this appeal has been admitted on 18.11.2024.

It appears from the previous order that on earlier occasion, the informant was made respondent No.2 and vide order dated 18.01.2025, learned co-ordinate Bench directed for issuance of notice on respondent No.2 on his present and permanent address under registered cover with A/D as well as Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1276 of 2024(12) dt.27-02-2026 ordinary process.
The notice could not be served and it was reported that respondent No.2 resides elsewhere and he was only a tenant on the given address.

4. It further appears that in the given circumstance, the learned co-ordinate Bench of this Court Brajesh Kumar @ Rahul vs The State Of Bihar on 27 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39863993/
1 passed order dated 16.04.2025 wherein the submission of learned counsel for the appellant has been recorded.

entities.text: Brajesh Kumar @ Rahul vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant made a submission that conviction has been recorded by the learned trial court under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code, therefore, the presence of the informant is not required looking to the facts of the present case.
He urged that he may be permitted to delete the name of respondent No.2 from the array of the party-respondents.
5. The learned co-ordinate Bench accepted the submission of learned counsel for the appellant and he was permitted to delete the name of respondent No.2-informant.

6. To this Court, it appears that learned counsel for the appellant was perhaps not aware of the order dated 30.04.2025 passed by this Court in Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 103 of 2019 (Heera Das Vs. The State of Bihar & Anr.).

entities.text: Heera Das Vs. The State of Bihar & Anr.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said appeal, the appellant had been held guilty for the offence punishable under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.1276 of 2024(12) dt.27-02-2026 Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
This Court, vide a reasoned order, has taken a view that the victim of the crime would be required to be heard and accordingly, directed that the informant be added as respondent No.2 in the appeal.
7.

Recently, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has taken same view in the case of X vs. The Sate of Uttar Pradesh & Anr. passed in Criminal Appeal No. 5385 of 2024 arsing out of SLP (Crl.) No. 5027 of 2024 along with Criminal Appeal No. 5386 of 2024 arsing out of SLP (Crl.) No. 5305 of 2024.

entities.text: X vs. The Sate of Uttar Pradesh & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
8. In the aforesaid view of the matter, we direct learned counsel for the appellant to add the informant as party-respondent No.2.
9.

Since the notices earlier sent to respondent No.2 could not be served upon him through ordinary and registered post, we direct that the appellant shall take steps for substituted service of notice by way of paper publication.
However, notice shall be published in such a manner that the name of the victim and/or his identity be not disclosed.
10. Office shall do the needful.
11. Learned counsel for the appellant shall file a copy of the notice published in the newspaper which has a Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.1276 of 2024(12) dt.27-02-2026 wide circulation in the area in which the informant resides and case is pending.

12. List this case on 30.03.2026 under appropriate heading.
(Rajeev Ranjan Prasad, J) ( Praveen Kumar, J) brajesh/-
